question: Q#115: CC over ssh is journaled as you. Measured on akiendelllinux: akienasus CC logs in with the same key (akien@akienasus) from the same host (10.0.0.68) your own ssh would use, and the CC environment (CAIRN_USER, CLAUDECODE) does not cross ssh, so 1002 commons and 669 cairn journal entries over ssh are classed akien. No approval has ever been journaled by anyone, so CC on akienasus has never approved over ssh. Which signal should tell CC-over-ssh from Akien-over-ssh at the artifact door: (a) a dedicated ssh key for CC on akienasus, read from the key sshd accepted; (b) akienasus CC sends LC_CAIRN_USER, which sshd already accepts (an asserted variable, the same trust as the CAIRN_USER rule that already counts); (c) every sshd session classes cc, which misclasses your own ssh; or something else? And until the signal exists, should artifact.approve and the operator close at trouble.py:307 refuse ANY sshd-session caller, your own ssh included, so you would approve only from a local desktop session?
why_it_blocks: caller() cannot class an sshd session correctly until the signal is chosen, and approve admits CC over ssh until then
answer: i agree on all counts. [on: (a) a dedicated ssh key for CC now; until it lands, approve and the operator close refuse any sshd-session caller; a claude_code user per box as the intention it grows into.] ... it wouldn't be 'run cairn as claude_code' it'd be 'run cairn as akien which launches the claude executable as claude_code'. ... cc is also allowed to use the inter-cc api to talk to each other, and 'reaching other devices' allows using ssh to get things set up and fix things like an IT admin. where possible you can login as claude_code over ssh and then launch claude executable.
